title: Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome in a Patient with Diabetic Ketoacidosis despite No Rapid Sodium Correction
case_prompt:
A 74-year-old Japanese man with alcohol-related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A), uncontrolled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c ~14%), and a 1-year history of abstinence from heavy drinking presented with acute wet cough and altered mental status (GCS E4V2M5). He was underweight (BMI 16.6) and a long-time smoker. 

On admission: T 36.4°C; HR 106 bpm; RR 20 bpm; BP 145/92 mmHg; SpO₂ 99% on room air. Exam: dry oral mucosa, gynecomastia. 

Initial labs: WBC 12,020/μL (Neu 88.7%); BUN 41 mg/dL; Cr 1.64 mg/dL; glucose 556 mg/dL; Na 127 mEq/L; measured osm 304 mOsm/kg; ketones 369 μmol/L; NH₃ 188 μg/dL; ABG: pH 7.382, pCO₂ 25.7 mmHg, HCO₃ 15.3 mmol/L, lactate 7.1 mmol/L, anion gap 20.5. CT chest: right middle and lower lobe ground-glass opacities; liver nodularity; no ascites.

He was diagnosed with DKA, community-acquired pneumonia, lactic acidosis, and prerenal AKI. Treatment: azithromycin, IV ceftriaxone, IV Ringer’s, continuous insulin infusion, rifaximin, lactulose, and amino acids. Over the first 24 h, glucose fell to 275 mg/dL, sodium rose to 135 mEq/L, osmolarity decreased to 295 mOsm/kg.

On hospital day 3, consciousness improved to GCS E4V4M6; insulin was switched to subcutaneous. On day 8, he re-deteriorated to GCS E4V2M5, with new dysphagia and chorea. Labs on day 8: WBC 10,440/μL (Neu 75.5%); glucose 138 mg/dL; Na 155 mEq/L. Neurologic exam revealed bilateral chorea of the head, trunk, and upper extremities; Babinski and Chaddock signs were negative; no myoclonus.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Diabetic striatopathy was considered because of poor glucose control around chorea onset — “Since the BG level was not well controlled around the chorea onset (130-322 mg/dL), we suspected diabetic striatopathy and hypernatremia as the causes…”  
2. Hypernatremia was considered due to the elevated serum sodium of 155 mEq/L — “Since the BG level was not well controlled around the chorea onset… we suspected diabetic striatopathy and hypernatremia as the causes…”  
3. Ceftriaxone-associated encephalopathy was considered given recent IV ceftriaxone therapy — “Based on the suspicion of differential diagnoses for altered mental status and chorea, including… CTRX-associated encephalopathy, … brain MRI was performed on day 11…”  
4. Hepatic encephalopathy was considered due to underlying cirrhosis and altered consciousness — “Based on the suspicion of differential diagnoses for altered mental status and chorea, including… hepatic encephalopathy, … brain MRI was performed on day 11…”  
5. Osmotic demyelination syndrome was considered given shifts in serum osmolarity and neurologic deterioration — “Based on the suspicion of differential diagnoses for altered mental status and chorea, including… ODS, brain MRI was performed on day 11… which did not reveal any abnormal findings.”
